analysis:
Both changed files are test-only: a new AutopilotTinyModelTests.swift (added, lines 1-243) and a small assertion addition in ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift (head lines 683-687). No production source, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, or authorization code is modified, so no threat-model control is weakened by this diff.

AutopilotTinyModelTests exercises the autopilot load/unload/hold paths against a synthetic tiny checkpoint in a temporary model cache. It uses test-only hooks (runAutopilotCommandForTesting, setIdleForTesting, setEngineV2SlotHooksForTesting, setDaemonStateFileForTesting) and a coordinatorURL of ws://127.0.0.1:0/ignored with attestationSigner nil, so nothing connects to a real coordinator. It touches no real secrets, and the weight-hash adoption requirement (T-012, T-027) is asserted rather than bypassed. It also asserts that adopted inventory is withdrawn on admin unload and after hold expiry, that stalled operations release KV reservations (T-010, T-029), and that autopilotServesModel is false after withdrawal. These are positive tests of existing behavior.

The ProviderModelSwitchTests addition asserts that .modelSwitch is not a busy reason after either failure and that .draining remains only when the commit is unconfirmed. This reinforces fail-closed admission and does not weaken it.

Remaining question for integration: the production behavior these tests cover (autopilot adoption/hold logic, superviseTransitions, autopilotBusyReasons, handleLoadModelRequest) is not in this batch. Any non-test change to those paths in other batches needs its own review. In particular, the test assertion that an adopted model keeps serving after lease expiry (lines 38-47) relies on production authorization semantics outside the supplied evidence.
